generator: analytics/run_all.py (generate → resolve → growth → forecast → stress → signals → streams → actions → business_case → build_summary)
growthFormula: Growth = PO value (Oct 2025–Sep 2026) ÷ PO value (Oct 2024–Sep 2025) − 1, per country × product, on de-duplicated customers (golden IDs). PO value in SGD for cross-product totals; PO units within a product.
seasonalityNote: We do not compare half-years: dengue season, fiscal-year flushes and CNY/Tet would make that seasonality, not growth.

params.forecastScope: Products A + B, all 5 countries, de-duplicated customers (golden IDs); cells weighted by S$ value

modelCard.purpose: Give regional management one consistent view of customer demand by country × product, show how much clean master data changes it, and test whether a seasonal forecast beats today's rolling average.
modelCard.intendedUse: Illustrative prototype on synthetic data. The same scripts are meant to be rerun unchanged on SAP B1 extracts (ORDR/RDR1, OQUT, OCRD, OITM) in week 1 of the pilot.
notIntendedFor: Real stock, budget or headcount decisions before the pilot re-measures every number on real orders
Forecasting Product C (instruments): it is planned from the tender / PR pipeline
Automatically merging SAP records: the matcher suggests, the MDM team decides

methods.name: Growth
methods.detail: Growth = PO value (Oct 2025–Sep 2026) ÷ PO value (Oct 2024–Sep 2025) − 1, per country × product, on de-duplicated customers (golden IDs). PO value in SGD for cross-product totals; PO units within a product. Momentum = PO value (Jul–Sep 2026) ÷ PO value (Jul–Sep 2025) − 1

methods.name: Entity resolution
methods.detail: Blocking: same recorded country and a shared Soundex code on any distinctive name word, or the same tax ID in any country; a record whose phone dialling code points to another country is also compared in that country. Score: the live intake scorer (src/lib/engine/dedupe.ts, ported 1:1 to Python and parity-tested): max(Jaro-Winkler, token-set ratio) on the normalised name (lowercase, punctuation and legal suffixes removed, abbreviations expanded), capped by how much of the distinctive wording both names share; the same tax ID lifts it to 0.97; same postcode, phone or company email domain add 0.03 each. Matches are grouped into golden IDs (transitive). Blocking design and threshold (0.905, the middle of the F1-best range) were chosen on SG+MY only, then frozen and scored once on TH/VN/MM. The duplicates were generated with typos, word reorder, romanisation, blank tax IDs and other address formats that the normaliser does not know about.

methods.name: Forecast
methods.detail: Fixed before any result was seen: 6 rolling origins (end of Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug 2026); horizons 1–3 months; 4 methods (rolling-6, rolling-12 = today's method, seasonal naive, damped Holt-Winters ETS); metrics WAPE and bias on PO units per country × product; headline = Products A + B on de-duplicated customers (golden IDs), each cell's units valued at its average S$ price so a reagent kit and a box of pipette tips count by value; Product C reported separately. At each origin every method is refit on data up to and including the origin month only, then scored on the next 1–3 months that exist (to Sep 2026): 15 scored points per cell (the Jul-2026 origin contributes h=1–2, Aug-2026 h=1). Leak test: overwriting every month after the origin with garbage leaves every forecast unchanged.

methods.name: Falsification
methods.detail: Our method doesn't invent signal: Products A + B, all 5 countries, golden IDs, S$-weighted WAPE; the identical pre-registered backtest (6 origins, horizons 1–3, refit at every origin) rerun on each dataset.

methods.name: Clean × method
methods.detail: Headline scope (Products A + B, all 5 countries, S$-weighted), the same pre-registered backtest as backtest.json. Rows change only the series the model is trained on: raw SAP records (recorded country × recorded product) or golden IDs (true country × true product). Both rows are scored against the same de-duplicated actuals, i.e. what each country really ordered. Raw differs from golden where misattribution (SG-coded duplicates of MY/VN hospitals from Jan 2026) and miscategorisation (reagent kits coded as Product B) shift the series.

methods.name: Signals
methods.detail: Drop-off: Apr–Sep 2026 vs the same months of 2025, a de-seasonalised trend and an overdue-reorder check (> 1.5 × the usual gap). Cross-sell: gap to similar customers (same country and type), sized to the customer's own spend; installed-base pull-through is a signal only, never a forecast feature (leakage).

methods.name: Inbox sorting
methods.detail: Transparent weighted rules (no model); scored once on a blind 60-message test set.

methods.name: Business case
methods.detail: Final model §6: hours × S$50, payback on hard hours only; soft and opportunity kept in separate columns.

limitations: All data is synthetic and the planted patterns are known in advance: good scores show the pipeline works and is honest, not that the patterns exist in Lives Group's data.

The de-duplicated view uses the generator's ground-truth golden IDs (the true picture the matcher aims at). The matcher's own crosswalk mis-clusters 8 of 388 records and recovers 61% of the S$1.06M misattribution (recovered: MY; missed: VN, the pairs shown as misses in the matcher evaluation). In production the view would use the matcher's crosswalk after MDM review.

The pre-registered backtest scores Apr–Sep 2026, the rise of the dengue season, where a rolling average lags most (today's method under-forecasts by 10%). A non-pre-registered rerun at the six off-season origins (end Sep 2025 – Feb 2026, scoring Oct 2025 – May 2026) gives 9.7 vs 9.5 per 100 (+0.2 points; ours wins 6 of 10 cells); over all 12 origins 10.5 vs 9.0 (+1.5 points). The gain is concentrated where the season turns, which is where today's method fails.
Forecast: ours beats today's method in 7 of 10 A/B cells and loses 3 (MY·A, TH·B, MM·B); on Product C it is worse (35 vs 31 per 100).
On uncleaned records the seasonal model is worse than today's method (15 vs 13 per 100): it learns the fake Jan-2026 level shift. Clean first.
P10/P90 bands are empirical (backtest actual ÷ forecast ratios pooled across countries), from only 6 origins.
Signal S$ are addressable before conversion, with team-assumed save (25%) and conversion (15%) rates.
Fixed illustrative FX rates; prices are order-of-magnitude list prices with no source.
The TypeScript matcher used at intake is a port of the same scorer (parity-tested on 25 fixture pairs); the live intake warns at 0.75 and blocks at 0.85, the batch merge threshold is 0.905.

dataHonesty.item: Customers, items, orders, PRs, enquiries, MDM history
dataHonesty.detail: Generated by analytics/generate.py from params.yaml with seed 42; all names fictional except the pinned demo record.
Shapes and the 2024 high → 2025 low taken from NEA / MOH / KKM case data (research log).
SG/MM Apr–Mar, MY/VN Jan–Dec, TH Oct–Sep; CNY / Tet / Songkran / Thingyan (research log).
Pre-registered, leak-tested (forecasts unchanged when future data is overwritten), losses reported; synthetic data only.

With seasonality and trend switched off our advantage is -0.6 points (within ±2, i.e. ≈ 0), so the method is not finding patterns that are not there. With a different seed and half the dengue effect it still wins by 2.3 points (smaller than the base 2.8, as expected with less seasonality).

dataHonesty.item: Season dependence of the forecast gain
dataHonesty.detail: Not pre-registered: off-season origins give +0.2 points, all 12 origins +1.5, vs +2.8 pre-registered.
Held-out TH/VN/MM: Of 100 duplicate warnings, 93 are real; Catches 87 of every 100 real duplicates. Perturbations not mirrored in the normaliser.
On 60 messages written without seeing the rules, the rules put 92 of every 100 in the right stream (88 of 100 on the 33 deliberately tricky ones). A person still confirms every routing.
Must be re-measured on 24–36 months of real B1 orders.
A13 assumes 6%; the pilot measures it on OCRD.

dataHonesty.detail: 25% / 15%, shown next to every S$ figure; never summed into revenue.
Team estimates and research-log prices; payback counts hard hours only (impact.json).

validatedHere: The pipeline runs end to end from one seed and reproduces (analytics/run_all.py)
The backtest is leak-free and its losses are reported
The matcher is measured on countries it was not tuned on
No advantage appears when there is no signal (falsification test)
Cleaning alone moves forecast error before any modelling (clean × method)
Business-case arithmetic reproduces the final model §6 figures
needsPilot: Hours saved per request (A19) and analyst hours (A21)
Bounce rate and median cycle time baselines (A13, A26)

pilotPlan.summary: 6-week pilot in SG + MY on the Customer and Item domains for SPD and QTS; rerun the analytics on SAP B1 extracts in week 1.
pilotPlan.scope: SG + MY · Customer + Item domains · SPD + QTS
steps: Week 1: extract ORDR/RDR1, OQUT, OCRD, OITM per entity database; run analytics/run_all.py unchanged on the extracts
Week 2: MDM team reviews the top 50 duplicate suggestions; measure real precision
Weeks 3–6: rerun the backtest monthly against today's rolling average; report losses too
Week 6: keep / kill on the KPIs: At week 6, if the median is above 6 business days or adoption is below 70%: fix or stop.

assumptions.text: Five countries: Singapore (HQ), Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Myanmar.
Entities: SPD sells Product A (diagnostics), QTS Product C (instruments), QTG Product B (lab essentials); large hospitals buy from all three, so each entity created its own customer record.
Products: A = IVD reagents and test kits (recurring, seasonal); B = lab consumables (steady); C = instruments (lumpy, tender-driven, fiscal-year flushes; each placement pulls through A).
SGD with fixed illustrative FX rates.
History Oct 2023 – Sep 2026 (36 months, amended so seasonal ETS has ≥2 full seasons); window Oct 2025 – Sep 2026; forecast Oct–Dec 2026; backtest origins end-Mar to end-Aug 2026.

Only confirmed POs are volume; PRs (quote accepted) are pipeline; enquiries are a leading indicator; follow-ups are excluded; MDM setup requests are internal work, linked to demand only as stuck demand.
Units within a product; SGD across products.
Growth (amended) = trailing-12-month YoY on de-duplicated customers; momentum = Jul–Sep 2026 vs Jul–Sep 2025. Half-on-half dropped: it would measure seasonality.
Approval matrix with parallel stage 1 (a policy change); conditional QA/RA for IVD items; Finance Director above S$50k credit.
SLA 2 business days per step in the approver's time zone; reminder after 1, escalation after 3; a question pauses the clock.
Baseline 18 calendar days for Amy's item (App C); target ≤4 business days median.
~80 MDM requests a month (customers incl. extend 35, items 30, vendors 10, cost centres 5); sensitivity 40 / 120.
40% of requests bounce at least once; 6% of new customer records are duplicates.
Production on Microsoft 365: canvas Power Apps + SharePoint List + Power Automate standard Approvals + Teams; only phase-2 SAP posting needs premium.
SAP B1 landing: phase 1 DTW import files loaded by MDM after the final check; phase 2 Service Layer via an SAP partner.
Sensitive fields (bank, credit limit, payment terms) visible to Finance and MDM only; reveals logged (UI-enforced in the prototype).
All data synthetic with documented planted patterns; National University Hospital exists only as a master record with no transactions.
Unit costs come from the verified research log, with sources.
1.25 h saved per request = rework 0.40 + forwarding/chasing 0.50 + manual keying 0.35 (team estimate).
4 h rework per duplicate customer; 70% intercepted at intake (team estimate).
Regional consolidation: 5 country analysts × 1 day a month = 40 h/month (team estimate).
Phase-1 build S$39,900 one-off (lean team S$24,000, contractor S$9,750, MDM config S$2,400, onboarding S$3,750); run cost 15%/yr.
Phase-2 SAP partner 15 days × S$1,500 = S$22,500 (low confidence).
10% leak rate on stuck demand (opportunity column only, never in payback).
FX USD 1 = S$1.33.
Baseline median cycle time 14 calendar days (Amy's case: 18).
